title: Role assignment can bind to the wrong account when the panel contains duplicate preset seats

finding.claim: Role assignment can bind to the wrong account when the panel contains duplicate preset seats
finding.evidence: The role-assignment code records the seat name returned by a fresh one-item build, then reuses any existing provider with that name instead of the actual seat selected by the main panel build. With duplicate presets, the main panel renames seats, so the role can point at a different account than requested.
finding.recommendation: Resolve role assignments against the already-built provider set instead of rebuilding the spec in isolation. For duplicate preset seats, either preserve the exact seat identity chosen during the main build or reject ambiguous role specs unless the user names a unique seat explicitly.

probe.summary: Duplicate-seat demonstration (`probes/duplicate_seat_probe.py`, result `duplicate-seat-78ddf4d5ea27.txt`): panel built from ['openai', 'openai'] pools two accounts under one seat; the pool sends the registry default 'gpt-5-mini' on both accounts. Applying --role correctness=openai:gpt-9.9-probe records role_models['correctness']['model'] = 'gpt-9.9-probe' while the seat object is unchanged and still sends 'gpt-5-mini' — the override callable is built, discarded on the name collision, and its model recorded anyway. The recorded model NEVER serves. Name-level half: seat names and pool sizes are identical across all spec orderings. Ruled jointly with #10 (same seam; #10's cross-kind guard does not cover a same-kind model override).
